Historically, this service facilitated connections between Liverpool and the Welsh resort en route to the Isle of Man, approximately three decades ago. According to restorer Steve Payne, funding for this endeavor is being sourced from private investors. Additionally, the project has benefited from fundraising efforts and received several bequests. The 55-meter-long vessel, initially launched in Hamburg in 1958, has languished in a state of disrepair at Liverpool docks since 1994, following a failed venture to convert her into a floating bar at Liverpool's renowned Albert Dock. A group of enthusiasts, led by Mr. Payne, rescued her from being scrapped in 2016 with the ambition of facilitating three-hour summer excursions for up to 450 passengers from Liverpool to Llandudno. The refurbishment will necessitate an overhaul of The Endeavour’s two diesel engines, while the lifeboats have already been dispatched to Norway for restoration. Numerous fittings require replacement, and the ship’s wheel has even been pilfered. Mr. Payne, who serves as secretary of the Liverpool and North Wales Steam Ship Company, noted that constructing a new ship of similar dimensions would currently incur costs between £25 million and £30 million. He emphasized that they possess the foundation of an exceptionally sound vessel. Mr. Payne is optimistic that the newly formed limited company will successfully fulfill the health and safety criteria essential for The Endeavour to depart from her berth at Liverpool's Canada Dock once more. Although The Endeavour lacks a history of sailing within British waters, Mr. Payne asserts that she is ideally suited for traditional summer day trips. On August 17, Planting Peace, a non-profit organization based in the United States dedicated to promoting peace in a troubled world, initiated a symbolic gesture near Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Utilizing a balloon equipped with a GoPro camera, the organization captured video footage as it ascended to an altitude of 21.1 miles (34.1 km) above the Earth's surface over a three-hour duration. The organizers intended this act as a peaceful and aesthetically pleasing declaration of space as inclusive and supportive of the LGBTQ community. The balloon, along with its attached flag, eventually returned to Earth, but not before producing striking images that depicted the planet's surface with the sun shining behind the flag. According to Planting Peace, the primary objective of this declaration is to advocate for the fundamental human rights of LGBTQ individuals, striving towards universal recognition that all individuals deserve to live and love freely without fear or discrimination. The organization further emphasized that this demonstration underscores the necessity for safe spaces for the LGBTQ community across all reaches of the universe. In addition to its advocacy for LGBTQ rights, Planting Peace is engaged in humanitarian aid efforts and environmental initiatives worldwide. The organization recently garnered attention during the Republican National Convention in Cleveland, Ohio, by displaying a provocative billboard featuring U.S. presidential candidate Donald Trump and then-aspiring Republican nominee Ted Cruz in a suggestive pose beneath the slogan "Love trumps Hate.

The programmes, once believed to be lost, were originally recorded by Everett for the early commercial radio station, Radio Victory. These recordings are distinguished by his signature homemade sound effects and jingles. Andy Ferris, a former presenter who unearthed these reels, remarked that they exemplify Everett's unwavering dedication to entertainment. Among the creative works included are "Sing-along-with-the-Beatles," "The Backward Contest," and the science fiction character Captain Kremmen. Mr. Ferris recently rediscovered these programmes within a collection of reels he acquired from the station following its licence revocation in 1986. At that juncture, Everett was a widely recognized figure due to his immensely popular television show. According to Mr. Ferris, Everett would send a weekly tape of one of his meticulously crafted programmes—each showcasing his humor, penchant for playful mockery, and preferred music interspersed with numerous sound effects. During this period, Everett's then-wife, Lee Everett Alkin, recalls him producing shows at their residence in Cowfield, Sussex, utilizing multi-track recorders to create what were considered pioneering effects at the time. She humorously recounts instances when she would be hosting tea only to be interrupted by startlingly loud sound effects emanating from down the corridor, leading them to eventually sound-proof his workspace. The Victory programmes, along with remastered versions of earlier BBC Radio Solent broadcasts, are set to be featured in an upcoming BBC documentary exploring Everett's life. Richard Latto, the producer of the documentary, observed that it is astonishing how contemporary the shows remain after so many years. On Monday, the parents of students at Tavistock and Summerhill, an independent school located in Haywards Heath, were informed via email that the institution would cease operations following the half-term break. A notice affixed to the school gate confirmed that the school had entered voluntary liquidation. The board of governors expressed regret over the closure and extended their gratitude to the teachers, parents, suppliers, and benefactors for their unwavering support. Elaine Prentice, a parent whose three-year-old daughter attended the nursery section of the school, lamented the unfortunate manner in which parents were treated, noting the distress among many of them. She remarked on the limited timeframe available to secure alternative schooling arrangements, stating, "We have only four days to find a new school." Prentice also criticized the governors for hiring new staff despite apparent financial difficulties known since September. A representative from West Sussex County Council advised parents seeking enrollment for their children in local maintained schools to contact the pupil admissions team, assuring that in-year applications are typically processed within ten school days. RSM Restructuring Advisory Ltd disclosed that it had been engaged to assist the school's directors in preparing for liquidation; however, it had not been officially designated as liquidator. The school accommodates 100 students from reception through year eight and an additional 50 in its nursery program. The email further revealed a significant decline in student enrollment over the summer months. Despite appointing a team to devise a sustainable financial strategy, the school could not maintain solvency long enough to implement it. Ms. Prentice also mentioned having prepaid £1,400 for her child's attendance at the nursery twice a week this term and now faces the challenge of reclaiming these funds from RSM UK in Crawley, acting as liquidator. The school board disclosed that several efforts had been made over the past five years to ensure the institution's long-term viability. Despite proposing various management alternatives throughout this year, each had ultimately been found unfeasible.

We believe we improved from our performance against Italy and can continue to improve further."

Jones expressed a need for refinement in specific areas: "We probably have five minutes to work on. It may sound repetitive, but if you look back a few years, we were probably saying the same thing. However, the majority of our performance showed significant improvement." Wales struggled initially in the first half against Italy but displayed a more cohesive team effort against England. Despite this, they were unable to maintain their lead as England capitalized on a Welsh error just before Daly scored.

Marine animals like porpoises, whales, and dolphins employ sophisticated echolocation techniques to hunt for prey, using clicks and buzzes to generate sound waves and interpret their echoes. Researchers from Aarhus University in Denmark have discovered that these animals adjust the focus of their acoustic signals—similar to altering the beam of a flashlight—from narrow to wide as they close in on their target. This adaptive mechanism may help prevent prey from evading capture. Moreover, these findings could lead to innovative strategies for mitigating the accidental entrapment of porpoises and other toothed whales in fishing nets. The study was led by Danuta Wisniewska and her colleagues, who conducted their research on harbor porpoises housed in a semi-natural enclosure along Denmark’s coast. This unique setup allowed the porpoises access to the seafloor while being separated from the harbor by a net, enabling them to hunt freely as fish entered the enclosure. The researchers equipped the porpoises with sound-detecting tags and installed an array of underwater microphones to record acoustic activity throughout the enclosure. These tools facilitated an in-depth analysis of how the porpoises directed their echolocation energy during hunting behaviors. In one experiment, fish were dropped into the water to prompt hunting activity, providing insights into how porpoises adjust their acoustic signaling during prey pursuit. The study revealed that harbor porpoises can expand their echolocation beam by up to 50% during the final phase of an attack. This flexibility is enabled by a specialized fatty structure in their forehead, known as the melon, which functions as an acoustic lens to fine-tune sound waves. The harbor porpoises involved in this research had been previously rescued after becoming entangled in fishing nets. The team hopes their findings will contribute to developing sound-based methods

Point One Marketing, operating under the name Stop the Calls, has been reported to engage in behavior characterized by intimidation and aggression. The Bournemouth-based company misleadingly presented itself as an official service for halting unsolicited calls. Consequently, the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) imposed a fine of £50,000 after receiving numerous complaints. Some individuals recounted being subjected to shouting when they requested not to be contacted again. Disturbingly, a woman afflicted with dementia was coerced into providing her credit card information. The ICO's head of enforcement, Stephen Eckersley, remarked that the company attempted to market a product purportedly designed to prevent nuisance calls, despite being largely responsible for such calls themselves. The manner in which they operated, marked by evident bullying and aggression, exacerbates the situation further. The legitimate means of stopping nuisance calls is through the Telephone Preference Service, which is available at no cost.

In response to a ransomware attack on NHS computer systems, Scottish ministers have urgently assembled a meeting of the National Cyber Resilience Leaders' Board. This initiative comes as Police Scotland collaborates with the National Crime Agency to investigate the breach, which targeted 11 health boards, NHS National Services, and the Scottish Ambulance Service. The cyber attack, first identified on Friday, disrupted services at acute hospitals in Lanarkshire as well as numerous GP surgeries and dental practices.

Justice Secretary Michael Matheson emphasized the necessity of heightened vigilance to prevent future incidents. He stated that the Scottish Government is proactively working to bolster cybersecurity measures by reaching out to over 120 public organizations to confirm their defense systems are robust. Matheson highlighted that email attachments and links from unknown sources are common vectors for such infections, urging individuals to exercise caution before interacting with them.

He also expressed gratitude to NHS staff and other organizations for their relentless efforts in managing this critical situation and minimizing its impact on patient care.

The commemoration at the city's war memorial was attended by former prisoner of war Len Gibson, who was captured in Singapore and forced to work on the infamous Burma Death Railway. A parallel ceremony took place at the Burma Star Memorial at St Thomas' Church in Newcastle. In London, the Queen and the Duke of Edinburgh presided over a remembrance service. Mr. Gibson, now 95, expressed his appreciation for the enduring recognition of such events, noting, "It's heartening to see that people still remember." Reflecting on his harrowing experiences, he remarked, "It was an atrocious time that remains etched in my memory—daily reminders surface that take me back to those days. We were treated as slaves by our Japanese captors. If we didn't work hard enough, they would beat us with sticks. We wouldn't have minded the labor if they had provided food, but instead, they starved us." Graham Hall, the chairman of the Sunderland Armed Forces Network and organizer of the memorial, emphasized the significance of remembrance. "It serves as a stark reminder of the inhumanity we continue to inflict upon each other," he stated.

The National Offender Management Service's annual reports have repeatedly failed to accurately reflect the number of prisoners living in overcrowded conditions. Specifically, they recorded that only one prisoner was living in a cell designed for a single occupant, when in fact, there were two. Prisons Minister Andrew Selous has described this oversight as unacceptable. Advocates emphasize the necessity of understanding the actual extent of overcrowding. 

In a written ministerial statement, Mr. Selous revealed that prisons have been reporting inaccurate data since 2008-2009. He stated, "The public rightly expects this information to be precise. Publishing clear and reliable data on the number of prisoners living in overcrowded conditions is crucial for accountability. It is therefore unacceptable that these inaccuracies have persisted for six years without detection." In response to these revelations, immediate measures have been implemented to ensure future data undergoes stringent quality control.

The Howard League for Penal Reform highlighted that this statement follows its research from two years prior, indicating that approximately 20,000 prisoners were housed in overcrowded conditions. Frances Crook, the League's Chair, remarked, "This timely statement is welcomed as it signals a new era of transparency and accountability within the Ministry of Justice. Simple logic dictates that if two or three prisoners are confined to a cell meant for one, all are experiencing overcrowding. We are pleased that government statistics will now accurately represent this fact—a point we have long advocated."

She further noted that holding inmates in cramped cells with no activities is counterproductive to their rehabilitation into law-abiding citizens upon release. Recognizing the true extent of overcrowding is vital; only then can effective solutions be developed collaboratively.

He subsequently sat on the ground to receive medical attention and did not continue playing. James Taylor assumed the captaincy in his stead. "He has a lump on his head, but he is fine," stated coach Trevor Bayliss. "He has a headache but is up and about now, engaging in conversation. When anyone gets hit, it's an anxious moment, but the fact that he walked off the field was reassuring. He experienced dizziness for a while and took about an hour to recover. I'm confident the medical staff will monitor him closely."

At this juncture, the hosts had already declined to 22-3 in the decisive match when Morgan was substituted by Jonny Bairstow, ultimately losing by eight wickets. The incident involving Morgan, who was wearing a helmet, elicited immediate concern among the visiting players, particularly as it occurred less than a year after Phillip Hughes's tragic demise. Hughes, an Australian batsman, passed away after being struck on the neck by a bouncer.

Fielders swiftly came to Morgan's aid, while a visibly shaken Mitchell Starc received comfort from captain Steve Smith, coach Darren Lehmann, teammate John Hastings, and Morgan's batting partner Ben Stokes. "There were a couple of guys who were quite shaken up, especially Starcy," Smith remarked. "It was a tough summer for us back home, losing a close friend. Whenever someone is hit like that, your primary concern is their health. My thoughts are with Eoin; I hope he recovers well."

Steve Smith further commented: "I don't think anyone ever intends for such incidents to happen; it is part of the game to bowl bouncers. You have to refocus as quickly as possible because you still have a job to do. Although you need to clear it from your mind, seeing someone get hit like that is distressing."

Notably, Kenya topped the medal table at the Olympic qualifiers earlier this summer. However, failing to qualify at this event does not preclude para-athletes from participating in Rio. It is merely one opportunity among several that will arise over the coming year. Additionally, under exceptional circumstances, such as this one, competitors may be extended invitations to compete. Furthermore, these championships are limited to athletics, meaning Kenya could still secure representation in other sports. Ms. Oluoch criticized her government's decision not to fund the para-athlete team as unjust. She remarked, "The able-bodied athletes had their World Championship in Beijing, and I believe the government supported it entirely. However, when it comes to para-athletes, they seem indifferent." Fifteen African countries are participating in the IPC World Championships held in Doha, Qatar's capital, including two athletes from Rwanda and 22 from South Africa.

She articulated a hope that the gravity of their deeds and the suffering they have inflicted will persist in their consciousness, highlighting the poignant irony that the duo still possesses each other's companionship. Their criminal trajectory eventually led to the murder of Mr. Cimone, purportedly motivated by apprehensions regarding potential eviction from a property he maintained, as previously disclosed during court proceedings. Authorities have identified Melhem as the individual responsible for killing two Israelis at a bar before fatally shooting an Israeli Arab taxi driver who transported him after the attack. In certain Scottish courts, such as Stirling, Kilmarnock, and Dundee, nearly 20% of women appearing before them are being sentenced to jail, a stark contrast to the 7% in Edinburgh and 5% in Airdrie. While the judiciary has deemed it inappropriate for an active sheriff to comment on this matter, retired Sheriff Peter Gillam provided insights from his extensive experience on the bench, having served from 1991 to 2013. He attributes these discrepancies to the inherent independence of the judiciary.

Sheriff Gillam noted that there is now a board established to advise judges on sentencing. However, he emphasized that judges are distinct individuals with varied perspectives and approaches, underscoring their autonomy in judicial decision-making. Although a level of consistency is maintained through the presence of an Appeal Court, which can rectify decisions deemed excessively deviant from accepted practices, he advocates for preserving judicial diversity.

Gillam remarked that diversity in judicial approaches enriches the legal process and cautioned against imposing rigid uniformity that may conflict with judges' informed discretion. He stressed the importance of trusting judges to leverage their local knowledge and comprehensive understanding of cases to render decisions to the best of their ability. Ultimately, he believes in allowing judges the latitude to exercise their judgment in accordance with their professional insights and personal convictions.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) confirmed that the problem was resolved at approximately 10:00 ET (14:00 GMT). According to the airline, the issue impacted up to 3,500 flights, a significant disruption that drew criticism from passengers and highlighted ongoing technical challenges faced by the carrier. In an official statement, United acknowledged the problem, saying, "We experienced a network connectivity issue this morning. We are working to resolve this and apologize to our customers for any inconvenience." The outage caused widespread delays, with passengers taking to social media to voice frustrations over a lack of timely updates. One traveler, Jeralyn Novak, tweeted: "Never flying @united ever again! The whole computer system is down and stuck in Boise." Similarly, journalist Betsy Fischer Martin shared that a United pilot described the situation as if "someone pulled the plug on our computers," adding, "It's embarrassing; I apologize." While United worked to restore flight operations following the FAA’s lifting of the ground stop order, reports of lengthy queues at airports across the country underscored the ripple effects of the disruption. This incident marks yet another technical setback for United in recent months. In June, a similar network connectivity issue resulted in flight cancellations and delays. Earlier in February, a software glitch caused first-class seats to be sold mistakenly for just $100 (£65). Although United attributed this error to a third-party software provider and declined to honor the fares, it faced backlash from affected customers. Such challenges are not unique to United Airlines. Other carriers have also grappled with technical difficulties. In April, American Airlines was forced to ground its planes due to an iPad software malfunction that prevented pilots from accessing flight plans. These recurring incidents within the aviation industry underscore the critical need for robust technological infrastructure

Alex Jackson, the head of campaigns at Dogs Trust, emphasized that dog waste is one of the most frequent complaints received by local authorities annually. He highlighted the simplicity of properly disposing of dog waste.

Network Rail's £50 million Great Western Electrification Programme is strategically designed to reduce travel durations on the route extending from London Paddington to Swansea. Rail passengers have been cautioned about potential disruptions throughout the summer period along this line. To facilitate the installation of overhead power lines, it is necessary to lower 10 kilometers of track east of the city and within the Box Tunnel, as well as to modify certain bridges. This includes adjustments to the track passing through Dundas Aqueduct, Box Tunnel, Middle Hill Tunnel, and Sydney Gardens, thereby preserving historical infrastructure, according to Network Rail. Additionally, eleven new sets of points will be installed. During these operations, replacement bus services will be available. Andy Haynes, Network Rail's project director for the West of England, emphasizes the critical nature of these preparatory activities in Bath for electrification readiness and extends his apologies to rail users. He acknowledges that many individuals plan to travel to and from Bath during the summer and assures them that Bath remains accessible for business, albeit with potentially extended travel times. From July 18 to July 31, the segment between Chippenham and Bath will be closed; however, services through Melksham will continue. In August, all lines east of Bath will be suspended for a month. Consequently, there will be no train service between Westbury, Freshford, and Avoncliff to Bath Spa, with journeys towards London from Bath Spa being redirected via Bristol Temple Meads and Parkway.

In November 2013, Essex Police received intelligence from the Child Exploitation and Online Protection Centre (CEOP) regarding Martin Goldberg. However, it wasn't until September of the following year that the police realized Goldberg was a teacher. Essex's police commissioner attributed the delay to the misinterpretation of an ambiguous phrase provided by CEOP. Although he refrained from specifying the phrase, Nick Alston indicated that this issue is currently under review by the Independent Police Complaints Commission (IPCC), and he emphasized that it would be inappropriate to speculate before the investigation concludes.

Martin Goldberg, who served as deputy head of Thorpe Hall School in Southend, was found deceased shortly after being interviewed by law enforcement. His name had been included in a list of 35 intelligence packages handed over by CEOP nearly ten months prior to his death. This information originated from Canadian police in 2012 following an inquiry into a company selling videos featuring naked children. Despite this, Goldberg was not flagged as high risk by Essex Police at the time.

Upon identifying Goldberg's occupation, officers sought a search warrant—ultimately denied—and proceeded to visit him at his residence. In response to this case, Mr. Alston stated that Essex Police has since revised its protocol. Now, upon receiving intelligence, immediate checks are conducted to ascertain if individuals work with children. Mr. Alston stressed the importance of quickly identifying any critical issues and taking prompt action to protect children from potential harm.

A spokesperson for CEOP declined to comment on the specifics of the case, citing the ongoing IPCC investigation.

Cisco further speculates that global revenues derived from Angler-related attacks may surpass $60 million. Subsequent research revealed that the poem, previously unpublished at the time of its writing, was later included in the 'Roald Dahl Treasury,' a 1997 anthology of formerly unpublished works. In commemoration of Dahl's centenary, both the letter and poem were exhibited at the school on Tuesday. **Sgt Robert Bye VC: Honoring a Welsh Hero**

Sgt Robert Bye, a distinguished Welsh Guardsman, was awarded the Victoria Cross (VC) for his extraordinary bravery on the opening day of the Third Battle of Ypres—commonly known as the Battle of Passchendaele—on July 31, 1917. To commemorate his legacy, a paving stone inscribed with his name is set to be unveiled during a special ceremony at Ynysangharad War Memorial Park in Pontypridd.

The remarkable valor demonstrated by Sgt Bye during one of World War I’s most grueling campaigns earned him widespread recognition. His actions were instrumental in securing key objectives for the Welsh Guards and led to the capture or elimination of 70 German soldiers. Upon returning home, he received a hero's welcome in Penrhiwceiber, where streets were adorned with bunting and schools closed to honor his achievements. Sgt Bye later transitioned to civilian life as a coal miner and passed away on August 23, 1962, at the age of 72.

### **Heroism at Passchendaele**

The Third Battle of Ypres was a brutal campaign marked by staggering losses; over 300,000 Allied casualties were reported, equating to 35 lives for every meter of territory gained. On the battle’s first morning, Sgt Bye’s company successfully overran the lightly defended German forward line but soon faced fierce resistance from heavily fortified blockhouses in the support line.

As the attack faltered under relentless machine gun fire, Sgt Bye took decisive action. Crawling alone toward the nearest blockhouse, he managed to neutralize its defenders with a hand grenade. When machine gun fire from a neighboring blockhouse turned on him, he evaded their bullets and silenced that position as well. His courageous and resourceful efforts allowed the Welsh Guards to secure their morning objectives—a feat that would not have been possible without his intervention.

He will collaborate with assistant coaches Matt Taylor and Dan McFarland, who are likewise affiliated with Townsend at the Warriors. Expressing enthusiasm for his new position, Blair remarked on the fortuitous timing amidst the team's evolving dynamics. As an emerging coach, he considers himself fortunate to engage with esteemed professionals such as Gregor Townsend and Dave Rennie, the forthcoming head coach of Glasgow Warriors, and aspires to contribute significantly to the future triumphs of both Scotland and Glasgow. Townsend will oversee the Warriors for the final time at Scotstoun in their concluding Pro12 match against Edinburgh, which also constitutes the second leg of the 1872 Cup. Subsequently, he will succeed Vern Cotter as Scotland's head coach, followed by the announcement of his squad for the summer tour of Italy, Australia, and Fiji. Blair, having earned 85 caps and participated in the British and Irish Lions tour in 2009, will accompany this touring ensemble while maintaining his commitments to the Warriors outside test-match periods. Townsend expressed that Mike Blair has excelled in his coaching endeavors since retiring from playing at the culmination of last season. Blair has demonstrated exceptional value to the Warriors' support staff, a skillset Townsend is eager to incorporate into Scotland's framework. Blair’s responsibilities with the national team will encompass three primary areas: facilitating offensive strategies, enhancing skill proficiency, and collaborating closely with the scrum-halves cohort.

The report "Caught Short" highlights a critical issue in India, where at least 48 million children under the age of five are stunted. This places India at the forefront of this global challenge, followed by Nigeria and Pakistan, which have 10.3 million and 9.8 million stunted children, respectively. Stunting is primarily a result of malnutrition during the crucial first two years of life and has lasting impacts on both physical and cognitive development. While inadequate food supply contributes to malnutrition, other significant factors include poor sanitation and contaminated drinking water. The report emphasizes that the lack of access to toilets, clean water, and proper hygiene practices exacerbates the problem. Recurrent diarrheal episodes, often stemming from unsanitary conditions and unsafe water, are directly linked to malnutrition and account for approximately 25% of all stunting cases within the first two years of a child's life. The scope of the issue in India is vast: about 76 million people lack access to safe drinking water, and 774 million live without adequate sanitation facilities. This situation is dire, with around 140,000 children succumbing to diarrhea annually. Open defecation remains a critical health challenge in India, which leads the world in this practice with over half a billion people affected. This practice not only spreads life-threatening diseases but also increases children's vulnerability to diarrhea and infections, as noted by Megan Wilson-Jones, WaterAid's policy analyst on health and hygiene. Despite these challenges, India has made some progress in reducing child stunting. In 2006, 48% of children were reported as stunted; by 2014, this figure had decreased to 39%, according to the charity’s findings. Henrique Capriles, a prominent Venezuelan opposition figure, articulated in an interview with the BBC that approximately 80% of the population was yearning for political change. He expressed confidence in his ability to gather four million signatures, a critical threshold required to trigger a recall referendum aimed at ousting President Nicolás Maduro. Highlighting the gravity of Venezuela's current predicament, Capriles remarked, "We are experiencing the worst crisis in our history." Venezuela's economic turmoil stems largely from its dependence on oil exports, which account for the majority of its revenue. The sharp decline in global oil prices, compounded by years of economic mismanagement, has plunged the nation into a state of near-total collapse. Last month, mass demonstrations—both in support of and against the government—drew hundreds of thousands of participants, underscoring the deepening divisions within Venezuelan society. Meanwhile, citizens across the country face mounting hardships, including widespread unemployment and severe food shortages, as exemplified by the dire conditions in industrial hubs like Valencia. The opposition attributes the nation's economic catastrophe squarely to Maduro and accuses the electoral commission of deliberately stalling efforts to organize a referendum that could curtail his tenure.
